dedupe_keys.name: opensidewalks schema pedestrian network data standard

description: The OpenSidewalks Schema is an open data standard for describing and sharing pedestrian transportation networks and pedestrian-adjacent data. It uses an explicit graph model: core entities are nodes, edges and zones for sidewalks, street crossings, curb ramps and other pedestrian paths, with adjacent entities such as points, lines and polygons, and custom entities; topology rules say, for example, that edges connect end to end and that curb interfaces are mapped at edge endpoints. Fields are a constrained interpretation of OpenStreetMap tags, so the schema is largely compatible with OpenStreetMap while also accepting agency or imagery-derived data. It is maintained by the OpenSidewalks project, with schema files hosted at sidewalks.washington.edu. It is generic and applies to any city. A JSON Schema for GeoJSON serialisation and a PostgreSQL schema are free on GitHub under Creative Commons Attribution-NoDerivatives 4.0. Caveats: it is a specification, not a dataset, and the no derivatives licence limits adapted versions of the schema text. It supports routable pedestrian networks for accessibility and evacuation modelling and agent-based pedestrian simulation. It complements the Japanese pedestrian network data (Hokonavi) and the Canadian cycling and pedestrian network databases catalogued here.
